corpus.name: gutenberg-mixed-narrative
corpus.description: The volume-matched control: the original 71 books plus 20.5 MB of further narrative prose, the same number of bytes the broad arm adds as drama, verse and non-fiction. Narrative stays near 93% of the corpus. Prepare it with --tokenizer-from pointed at the broad arm.
corpus.text_license: Public domain in the United States: every title was published before 1929 and its author died more than 70 years ago, so no copyright subsists in the text itself.
corpus.file_license: The Project Gutenberg files carry PG's own licence, which governs the PG header, footer and trademark rather than the work. That boilerplate is stripped here and never trained on, which is the condition PG states for using the text as an ordinary public-domain work. GITenberg's repository metadata is CC0/MIT.
corpus.restrictions: Literary English of 1320-1922, mostly British and American, with ten works in translation. It is not contemporary text, it is not balanced across dialects or demographics, and several works contain racial slurs, antisemitism and other period prejudice that a model trained on them will reproduce. The additions widen the period and the register but not the demographics.

split_policy.method: per document, contiguous, boundaries snapped to a blank line
split_policy.rationale: A shuffled split leaks overlapping context windows across the boundary. Splitting each document contiguously and in the same proportions avoids that leak and also keeps every author present in every split, so validation measures language modelling rather than domain transfer.

audit.note: Project Gutenberg header/footer boilerplate is removed before this scan; what remains is body text. No further records were removed. The duplicate rate is reported so the decision is visible.
